about: How learner projects are auto-graded. Checks come from grader/run_checks.py (run in a sandbox on GitHub Actions); the rubric is scored by Claude reading the repo. Points are out of 100.

checks.label: README explains how to run it
No keys or connection strings committed

rubric.label: Meets the brief
rubric.guide: Postgres calls table, a Python API with GET and POST /calls, a React page that lists calls, all deployed. Compare with the checks and the code.

rubric.label: Code quality
rubric.guide: Readable structure, input validation on POST, sensible error handling, no dead code dumps.

rubric.label: Secrets and safety
rubric.guide: Connection string read from the environment, .env ignored, a .env.example with blanks, parameterised SQL.

rubric.label: README and submission
rubric.guide: Someone new could run it from the README. The curl and Postman requests in the submission match the API.

checks.label: README explains how to run it
No LiveKit or model keys committed
The bot's prompt is in the repo

rubric.label: Prompt fits a real use case
rubric.guide: A short, specific prompt for a real job such as qualifying a loan lead: goal, tone, what to collect, when to stop.

rubric.label: Voice pipeline
rubric.guide: STT, LLM and TTS (or a realtime model) wired with the Agents framework; turn detection and interruptions considered.

rubric.label: Notes on 3 setting changes
rubric.guide: Three distinct changes (voice, turn detection, interruption...), each with what changed, what they expected and what happened.

rubric.label: README and hygiene
rubric.guide: Run steps, keys only in .env, .env.example present.
